obligations.subject: actor-model semantic floor
obligations.question: Verify Hewitt, Agha, Agha and collaborators' later functional and algebraic actor work, formal lambda-calculus actor foundations, and other premium primary actor-system research; distinguish their laws from Bombay constructions and policy. Exclude generic reactor/event-loop work.
obligations.decision: Semantic floor verified against primary sources. Actor-model LAWS adopted: (1) one communication at a time per actor (Agha 1986; Clinger 1981); (2) transition effects are exactly send/create/become (Agha 1986; AMST 1997); (3) fresh address allocation at creation (Agha 1986; AMST 1997); (4) acquaintance-based addressing (Hewitt-Bishop-Steiger 1973). DERIVED: Bombay's creator-local nonce, typed event sums, SendAlgebra monoid, typed observation lanes. POLICY: creation-before-same-transition-sends ordering, supervision vocabulary, shutdown lane. Generic reactor/event-loop literature (SEDA, libevent, Netty) was excluded from authority per the goal.

obligations.subject: fresh allocation and become
obligations.question: Verify primary-source distinctions between creation, fresh address allocation, and behavior replacement.
obligations.decision: Verified. LAW (Agha 1986 ch. 3-5; AMST 1997 sec. 2-4): creation allocates a mail address fresh with respect to the configuration and installs an initial behavior; become replaces the current actor's behavior only and never allocates. The two operations are orthogonal in the operational semantics. DERIVED (Bombay): Create carries a creator-local nonce so the creating transition can refer to its staged child without performing allocation in the pure fold; CreationKind records lifecycle provenance as data. POLICY (Bombay): interpreters install a transition's creates before interpreting that transition's sends and local observation requests; replacement at an existing address is deliberately absent and stable identity is derived via a proxy actor.
evidence: Agha, Actors: A Model of Concurrent Computation in Distributed Systems, MIT Press, 1986, ch. 3 (create task: new mail address plus initial behavior) and ch. 5 (become as replacement behavior)
Agha, Mason, Smith, Talcott, A Foundation for Actor Computation, J. Functional Programming 7(1), 1997 (fresh address names in labeled transitions; no address reuse)
Clinger, Foundations of Actor Semantics, MIT AI-TR-633, 1981 (newly created actors have previously unused addresses)

validation: Distinction cross-checked against the two independent primary semantics (Agha 1986 task-based, AMST 1997 lambda-based) which agree on fresh allocation vs behavior replacement

obligations.subject: law/derivation/policy map
obligations.question: Classify every semantic claim retained in the research report and implementation.
obligations.decision: Classification map established and applied across REPORT.md and every resolved obligation/capability row. LAW (research-mandated): one-communication-at-a-time; send/create/become effect triple; fresh allocation; acquaintance addressing; become distinct from allocation; per-actor serialization. DERIVED (Bombay constructions grounded in the laws): creator-local nonce routing; typed nested event sums with extraction traits; SendAlgebra monoid and SendProduct lanes; BirthMode/NoBirths/Births compile-time creation capability; proxy-derived stable identity; CreationKind provenance; timer generation pairs; stash replay discipline; Fsm phases. obligations.subject: small compositional basis
obligations.question: Show which minimal sums, products, folds, and transformations generate the pure capability catalogue.
obligations.decision: The generating basis is seven constructs: (1) the Behavior fold (Event -> Result<Actions, Error>) with init as the explicit initial observation; (2) typed concrete sums for event lanes (AtEvent, ReceiveTimeoutEvent, WatchEvent, ShutdownProtocol, SupervisionEvent) with extraction traits (UserEvent/TimeEvent/PeerEvent/ChildEvent/WorkerEvent/ShutdownEvent); (3) typed products for independent effect seats (Actions { Sends: SendAlgebra, creates: Vec<Create>, become_: Step }) and SendProduct for lane products; (4) the uninhabited Never closing phase/outbound/offspring menus; (5) BirthMode as the type-level creation capability; (6) non-capturing function pointers for reactions (At/ReceiveTimeout/Link/Shutdown/SupervisionFailure); (7) higher-order wrapper composition (At, ReceiveTimeout, Watching, Supervising, Stashing, Fsm, shutdown wrappers, Spec). Generation: 30 rows are existing basis instances, 13 are derivations, 0 new primitives, the remaining 10 rows are interpreter/application boundaries that the basis deliberately does not generate.

obligations.subject: failed derivations and missing primitives
obligations.question: Attempt derivation before adding primitives; document exact algebraic/type obstruction and validate every retained addition.
obligations.decision: No primitive was added: every derivation either succeeded or terminated at an explicit, recorded boundary. Boundary obstructions (why derivation stops, not what to add): backpressure — the model's mail queue is unbounded (Agha 1986), so throttling needs queue-depth observation that a one-event fold must not have; fairness — quantifies over executions (Clinger 1981), cannot be behavior-local; persistence/durable-state — I/O is outside the send/create/become effect triple; remoting/serialization/distribution — transport and wire representation are interpreter realization of already-typed Delivery values; scheduling/resource-ownership — executor and lifetime authority. These are recorded as interpreter/application dispositions with the exact obstruction in each row's composition field. Zero new-primitive rows remain; the survey found no gap in the reusable pure algebra.

obligations.subject: actorpass as consumer validation
obligations.question: Map actorpass interpretation to the completed algebra without allowing it to define or limit behaviorpass.
obligations.decision: Actorpass is mapped as one interpreter of emitted Actions values, and nothing in this campaign let it define or bound the algebra. Interpretation contract consumed by an actorpass-style runtime: (1) install every Create before interpreting the same Actions' sends and local service requests (documented on Actions); (2) per-lane order preserved, cross-lane order free; (3) resolve ScheduleAt/ScheduleAfter against its clock, mint TimerElapsed with the carried TimerId+TimerGeneration; (4) serve ObservePeer/ObserveChild requests and publish PeerStopped/ChildStopped only for committed actors; (5) deliver ReportWorkerStopped to the proxy's parent as WorkerStopped with the proxy nonce supplied; (6) mint Crash when execution ends without Exit; (7) inject ShutdownRequested when its policy says so. Validation of the algebra came from actorpass's needs (proxy supervision, workers! fleets, receive timeouts) as exercised in the testkit — but the algebra's laws above are derived from the primary sources, and interpreter-only capabilities (fairness, scheduling, backpressure, remoting) stayed out of the fold even though actorpass will own them.
